data.plinth_note: PLINTH HEIGHT IS A FAMILY FACT, not a global standard. CESAR - 1 Project Guidelines.pdf prints the dimension chain '78 H. Cesar door' over '10 Plinth H.' on printed p.73 (handles) and again on p.82 (grip recesses, where the door reads 75 and the plinth still 10), giving 780 + 100 = 880 to the worktop underside. H.84 prints 6 on printed p.90 and N_Elle repeats both pairings on p.175 and p.186 - so it tracks the HEIGHT FAMILY, not the collection. DECLARED HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE for family H.78: the loader merges non-unit_types keys last-file-wins across the three files that share this family name (appliance_h78, base_h78, sink_base_h78), so a second copy would be both a second thing to change and a silent clobber if the two ever disagreed. tools/test_contract.rb reads it back through Registry.lookup for a code out of each of the three files.

door_versions.note: The two door heights printed over a single code table: 78 full, 75 when the top 30 mm goes to the gola profile. FAMILY-SCOPED - the manifest's door_version axis says 'each base-unit page', and a family that does not declare this key has no such choice. Wall H.36 is 360 tall and 78/75 means nothing there.

data.source_ref: CESAR - 2 Kitchen System.pdf printed p.36-43 / PDF 38-45
page_observations: THE CATALOG PRINTS TWO PICTOGRAMS PER DEPTH ROW AND WE HAD NEVER READ THEM. printed p.19 carries the legend: a small cabinet-in-bracket glyph is 'Hung version' and a flame on a burner is 'Provisions for hob'. They sit beside each d.35 / d.62 / d.67 band in every base code table. FOUND 2026-08-23 while extracting printed p.37, five days after the first base page was read, because that page is the first to print a position that CANNOT be hung. The hob mark is recorded from here on as hob_provisions_depths_mm; on printed p.37 and p.38 it is on d.62 and d.67 and never on d.35, which is what a hob needs depth for. A SWEEP OF printed p.36, p.39, p.40 AND p.42 IS OWED - their rows were transcribed without either mark, so absence there means unread, not absent.

AND THE HUNG MARK IS A PRINTED FACT THE ENGINE DERIVES. Generator.wall_hung_available? says every base and tall cabinet can be hung unless a row says otherwise; printed p.37 prints two positions that say 'not available wall hung' in words, and their left margin drops the 'Surch. for wall-hung version on page 548' line that every other base position carries. Checked across printed p.36, p.39 and p.40: every extracted position there does carry the surcharge line, so nothing already held is wrong - the derivation was right by luck and is now backed by a flag on the two articles that break it.

ONE DESCRIPTION, TWO ARTICLES, TWICE ON ONE PAGE. printed p.38 prints 'Base unit with drawer and doors' as suffix 40 AND as suffix 46, and 'Base unit with drawer and door' exists as 41 on printed p.37 and 47 on printed p.38. The words are identical and so are the widths, depths and - for 40 against 46 - the prices in every band. WHAT SEPARATES THEM IS THE ELEVATION: 40 and 41 print two, a handle 19,5/58,5 and a gola 16,5/55,5; 46 and 47 print one, 19,5/55,5 with the groove between the fronts and none under the worktop. Anything that keys a position by its printed description would merge two articles the factory sells apart.

TWO SHAPES THIS REGISTRY CANNOT YET DRAW, AND THEY ARE CONTRACT GAPS, NOT PAGE PROBLEMS. (1) A band above a split: a drawer front across the full width with TWO doors beneath it. front_layout v2.1 has single, vertical_split, horizontal and corner_door, and none of them nests, so Export.fronts_in would count two fronts where the page prints three. (2) An article printed only in the gola execution: 19,5 + 55,5 = 750, the family's gola door height, where a handle execution must sum to 780 - and door_versions is a FAMILY key, so there is no way to say that one code exists at 75 and not at 78. Thirteen of the twenty-eight codes on these two pages are held and not buildable for one or both reasons.

base_corner.description: Corner base unit - 1 rh or lh door, 8x8 fixed corner front panel, 1 shelf
base_corner.source_ref: printed p.42 / PDF 44; confirmed against printed p.10 (technical and dimensional information)
base_corner.notes: THE HAND IS PART OF THE CODE ON THIS PAGE, AND IT IS NOT THE HINGE. SCOPE, narrowed 2026-08-20: what follows is a corner-page reading, not a catalog-wide law - see the CAUTION below. The page prints every row as '...D/S' - Destra / Sinistra - and the letter names the EXECUTION of the cabinet: which end carries the door and the 8x8, and which end is blind with the wasted space behind it. S is the one drawn on the page (door at the left end, 8x8 immediately right of it); D is its mirror. A corner carcass is not symmetric, so the mirror cannot be had by turning the unit around - it is a different article, and both are needed in a U-shaped kitchen, one per corner. The 'LH' beside the drawing is something else entirely: it is the DOOR's hand, the ordinary per-order hinge_side, which does not change the code. Confirmed with Andriy 2026-08-17. Printed rules, verbatim: W.100/105 unit with 30 cm door - 90 cm carcass; W.115/120 unit with 45 cm door - 90 cm carcass; W.130/135 unit with 60 cm door - 120 cm carcass. The W notation is the space the corner NODE occupies, not the box: the second number is the unit's own depth + 80 (the 8x8 filler projecting forward), the first is the nominal length along the door wall. Nominal, in cm, with the 3 mm gaps not counted. Nominal minus the carcass length is WASTED SPACE - the unreachable depth of the corner, which must stay free and is drawn as edges only. CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY on printed p.10 ('overall dimensions of corner base units', Technical and dimensional information), read 2026-08-17: the same three rules ('30-cm door for 95x65, 100x70, 105x75 base units, 90-cm carcass' and so on) plus a plan diagram. The diagram is labelled RH and shows the corner on the LEFT, the door at the RIGHT end, the 8x8 filler immediately left of the door, and the blind wasted zone further left behind the returning run - which is exactly our D execution mirrored from S. So RH (as drawn on p.10 and p.11) = D = destra = door at the right end. The engine's geometry matched the drawing with no change. CAUTION: p.10/p.11 draw the node RH while p.42 draws the same article LH, so on THIS page the hand cannot be read off a picture. The GENERAL form of that rule is dead as of 2026-08-20: factory estimate 2026/30829 orders PD0631 with OPENING DIRECTION: Left (rows 15, 25) and with Right (rows 18, 27) - one code, both hands - so for a ..31 wall unit the hand is an order variant and is not in the code at all. That closes Elda Q7a. What stays open is Q7b, and only for corners: does the execution letter behave like the wall-unit hand, i.e. is it a variant on one article rather than two articles? The corner CARCASS is genuinely handed - that is geometry, and no estimate can change it - but WHERE the handedness is recorded is unsettled. Generator.swap_corner_execution! currently rewrites the code; if Q7b comes back the other way it must rewrite a variant field instead. The placement gesture is unaffected either way. Estimate 30829 contains no corner unit, so it neither confirms nor refutes this. p.10 also names a THIRD corner depth we do not hold: 95x65 / 110x65 / 125x65, i.e. d.57 (65 = 57 + 80). It is absent from p.42 and we have not found the page that prices it, so it is recorded as a gap, not guessed. p.10 further states when the 8x8 is mandatory: 'Fit corner base units with 8x8-cm fillers adjacent to drawer units, jumbo drawers and dishwashers (or custom-sized corner base units).'

front_layout.note: One door of 300/450/600 at the execution's end, then the 8x8 corner filler: ONE solid L, both legs 80 long and 22 thick, its front leg on the door plane and its return projecting forward so the perpendicular run meets it. The rest of the carcass front is blind. Door and filler share the front height, so door version 75 shortens both.

base_door_pull_out_table.wall_hung_note: PRINTED, NOT DERIVED: 'not available wall hung' is the page's own last line, and the left margin of this position omits the 'Surch. for wall-hung version on page 548' that every other base position carries. Generator.wall_hung_available? assumes every base and tall CABINET can be hung and reads this flag as the only way out - so this is the first article in the registry to exercise it. See the page_observations note on the printed pictograms.
base_door_pull_out_table.notes: THE HEADING CARRIES A TYPO AND IT IS KEPT: the page prints 'pull-out tabe' in the heading and 'pull-out table' in the line below it, on the same position, twice on the page. The registry keeps the catalog's words. One code, one width, d.62 only. The 97 cm table is longer than the 60 cm carcass, which is why it pulls out.

front_layout.note: Elevation printed p.37: 19,5 / 58,5, summing to 780 - the HANDLE execution, and the only one this position prints. Top band is the table's own front, bottom band the door. NO gola_stack: the page prints no second elevation for this position and states 'no intermediate grip recess', so what the gola execution looks like is stated in words and not in numbers. Rule 8 - the numbers are not guessed from the twin position four rows down.

base_doors_pull_out_table.not_buildable_reason: THE FRONT IS A BAND ABOVE A SPLIT AND front_layout HAS NO WORD FOR THAT. This position is one 195 table front across the full width, with TWO doors of 585 below it - a horizontal band whose lower band is itself split vertically. Contract v2.1 offers single, vertical_split, horizontal and corner_door, and none of them nests. Recorded as horizontal [195, 585] so the heights are not lost, and marked incomplete so nothing draws it: Export.fronts_in would count TWO fronts where the page prints THREE, and a handle count that is quietly wrong is worse than one that is refused. THE CONTRACT GAP IS THE FINDING, not this article.

base_drawer_door_gola_only.description: Base unit with drawer and door - 1 drawer - 1 rh or lh door - 1 shelf
base_drawer_door_gola_only.not_buildable_reason: THE PAGE PRINTS ONE ELEVATION AND IT IS NOT THE FULL-HEIGHT ONE: 195 + 555 = 750, the family's GOLA door height, with the groove drawn between the two fronts and none under the worktop, so 780 - 750 = 30 is the single intermediate recess. THAT READING IS OURS (rule 4), forced by arithmetic: a handle execution must sum to 780 and this does not. And door_versions is a FAMILY key - full_mm and gola_mm are stated once for H.78 and every article inherits both - so there is no way yet to say this code exists at 75 and not at 78. Held, findable, orderable, and not drawn until that axis can be narrowed to an article.
base_drawer_door_gola_only.notes: SUFFIX 47, the twin of 41 four rows up on the previous page. Identical description, identical widths, identical depths, different price and a different elevation. The type key says what the elevation says and the word 'gola' appears nowhere on the page.

front_layout.note: NO heights_mm_top_to_bottom: the page prints no full-height elevation for this article, and inventing one from its twin is exactly what rule 8 forbids. The gola stack below carries the printed numbers, and Export.horizontal_fronts already falls back to it for the front count.
